floor_history.headline: Recon: floor 24 confirmed (75 vs 77 insns); residual isolated to 4 families; named-intermediate lever reaches 77/77 insn parity (score 33) and biv-elimination confirmed as the cause of the folded stor
Floor 24 -> 20: D1 and D3 both closed and target's exact register assignment reached at build_insns 77 == target_insns 77; residual is the $v0/$v1 mirror in the if-arms plus preheader order.

Floor held at 20 (77/77 insns); eleven structural variants measured and killed, and D2's mechanism corrected from a local-alloc combine_regs tie to a global.c allocno_compare contest between exactly t

Floor 20 -> 18: a permuter-found, hand-minimised per-loop carrier re-home (the 0x20-bits_left shift amount computed into the other bit loop's dead walking pointer, plus a second holder for 'needed') c

Floor 18 -> 12 and D2 (14 pts, the $v0/$v1 mirror that blocked sessions 1-4) is CLOSED: giving `hi` two extra refs per arm crosses the floor_log2 bucket in global.c allocno_compare and hands it $v1, a

frontier.hypothesis: D6 (4 pts) closes by ADDING references to the third loop's address walker `out` so it outranks `val` and is allocated first (taking $v0), rather than by demoting `val` - the exact mirror of the session-5 win, and the only direction not yet measured dead.
frontier.mechanism: global.c allocno_compare priority floor_log2(nrefs)*nrefs/livelen. Target emits `li $v1,-2` + `addiu $v0,$t3,0x348`, i.e. `out` is allocated before the -2 holder. `val` (holding the -2) is nrefs 19 / pri 50666; `out` has roughly 6 refs, so it needs the same floor_log2-bucket crossing that `hi` just made. Every attempt to demote `val` instead costs D1 (measured five ways this session).
frontier.next_probe: Route the third loop's store through `out` the way the bit loops now route through `hi` - e.g. give `out` an extra def-use per iteration that a human would write anyway - and read the ALLOCDBG pri column (tmp/grind/func_8001979C/s3/qty.sh) rather than only the sandbox score, since it shows how close a form came to flipping the order.

frontier.hypothesis: D5 (4 pts) is a list-scheduler tie-break, not a source-order effect, so it must be attacked with the sched.c model rather than by moving statements.
frontier.mechanism: Target emits `sllv $a2,$a2,$a0` (`cur <<= needed`) before the `or`; we emit the `or` first. Moving the C statement above the store is bit-identical (vTieShiftEarly, 12), so the decision is made in sched.c's INSN_PRIORITY ordering of the arm's ready list.
frontier.next_probe: Point tools/sched_solver (validated 6978/6978, memory/project/sched-solver-campaign-2026-08-05.md) at the arm's block in both our build and target, identify the priority/tie-break that orders the `or` against the `sllv`, then derive which C-visible change (an extra dependence into `cur`, a different consumer distance) moves it.

frontier.hypothesis: D4 (4 pts) - the walker init's preheader position - has never been attacked through loop.c itself; both source-level levers are now measured dead at two different allocations (P6 at floor 20 -> 31, vTieLateInit at floor 12 -> 27).
frontier.mechanism: loop.c move_movables / scan_loop choose the preheader insertion point; global.c allocno_compare fixes what may move (counter nrefs 21 / livelen 60 / pri 14000 against walkers at nrefs 13).
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/loop.c move_movables / scan_loop and determine where the insertion point is chosen relative to the loop's first insn and whether the walker init is a movable at all in this form; only then re-test a late init.
